answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by hunting lockstep behaviour, not just counting heads. A controller running many sockpuppets leaves a timing fingerprint: its identities wake, trade and vote in near-perfect synchrony, like pigment swirling from a single inlet into one stream. Genuine agents are messier, their rhythms drift, pause and diverge. So score each identity by how correlated its activity is with others over many epochs; clusters that move as one basalt block get throttled as a single actor, their voting weight collapsed, until their behaviour proves genuinely independent.
